use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};
use crate::orchestrator_v2::task_graph::TaskGraph;

pub fn validate_graph(graph: &TaskGraph) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut indegree = HashMap::new();

    for (id, node) in &graph.nodes {
        indegree.entry(id.clone()).or_insert(0);
        for dep in &node.deps {
            *indegree.entry(dep.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
        }
    }

    let mut queue = VecDeque::new();
    for (node, degree) in &indegree {
        if *degree == 0 { queue.push_back(node.clone()); }
    }

    let mut visited = 0;
    while let Some(node) = queue.pop_front() {
        visited += 1;
        if let Some(n) = graph.nodes.get(&node) {
            for dep in &n.deps {
                if let Some(v) = indegree.get_mut(dep) {
                    *v -= 1;
                    if *v == 0 { queue.push_back(dep.clone()); }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if visited != graph.nodes.len() {
        return Err("GRAPH_CYCLE_DETECTED".into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub struct Heartbeat;

impl Heartbeat {
    pub fn ignite(tx: broadcast::Sender<String>, monitor: Arc<Mutex<SystemMonitor>>) {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            loop {
                sleep(Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
                
                let vitals = {
                    let m = monitor.lock().await;
                    m.get_vitals()
                };

                let pulse = serde_json::json!({
                    "type": "VITALS_UPDATE",
                    "payload": vitals
                });

                let _ = tx.send(pulse.to_string());
            }
        });
    }

// inquisitor.rs — v1.1 [UI_AUDIT_RESTORED]
// Autonomous workspace auditor. Called by SelfHealingEngine on each cycle.
use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::SystemTime;
use tokio::process::Command;

pub struct Inquisitor;

impl Inquisitor {
    /// audit_ui: Checks for missing critical Svelte/UI files.
    pub async fn audit_ui() -> anyhow::Result<String> {
        let critical_paths = ["ui/src/App.svelte", "ui/package.json", "ui/index.html"];

        for path in critical_paths {
            if !Path::new(path).exists() {
                return Ok(format!("FRACTURE: Missing critical UI file: {}", path));
            }
        }

        if !Path::new("ui/node_modules").exists() {
            return Ok("FRACTURE: UI dependencies (node_modules) missing. Run npm install.".into());
        }

        Ok("NOMINAL".into())
    }

    /// audit_backend: Runs `cargo check` and returns errors or "NOMINAL".
    pub async fn audit_backend() -> anyhow::Result<String> {
        let output = Command::new("cargo")
            .args(["check"])
            .output()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Cargo check failed: {}", e))?;

        if output.status.success() {
            Ok("NOMINAL".into())
        } else {
            Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string())
        }
    }

    /// diagnose_workspace: Runs both audits and returns a combined report.
    pub async fn diagnose_workspace() -> anyhow::Result<String> {
        let backend = Self::audit_backend().await.unwrap_or_else(|e| e.to_string());
        let ui = Self::audit_ui().await.unwrap_or_else(|e| e.to_string());

        if backend == "NOMINAL" && ui == "NOMINAL" {
            return Ok(
                "WORKSPACE_NOMINAL: Integrity verified across Rust and Svelte domains.".into()
            );
        }

        let mut diagnostic = String::from("WORKSPACE_FRACTURE_DETECTED:\n");
        if backend != "NOMINAL" {
            diagnostic.push_str(&format!("--- BACKEND ERRORS ---\n{}\n", backend));
        }
        if ui != "NOMINAL" {
            diagnostic.push_str(&format!("--- FRONTEND ERRORS ---\n{}\n", ui));
        }

        Ok(diagnostic)
    }

    /// probe_shadow_activity: Detects files modified in the last 60 seconds.
    pub fn probe_shadow_activity() -> Vec<String> {
        let mut alerts = Vec::new();
        let targets = ["./src", "./ui/src"];

        for path in targets {
            if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(path) {
                if let Ok(modified) = meta.modified() {
                    if let Ok(elapsed) = SystemTime::now().duration_since(modified) {
                        if elapsed.as_secs() < 60 {
                            alerts.push(format!(
                                "SHADOW_ACTIVITY: {} modified recently ({}s ago)",
                                path,
                                elapsed.as_secs()
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        alerts
    }
}

use std::process::{Command, Output};
use std::io::Result;

pub struct IsolationJail;

impl IsolationJail {
    // Dynamically detect if we are running in the Motorola/Termux environment
    fn is_termux() -> bool {
        std::env::var("PREFIX").map(|p| p.contains("com.termux")).unwrap_or(false)
    }

    pub fn execute(command: &str) -> Result<Output> {
        let cmd = command.to_lowercase();
        
        // 1. The Emancipation List: Native execution for safe Rust/Cargo pipeline ops
        let host_allowed = [
            "cargo ", "rustc ", "ls ", "cat ", "grep ", "find ", "git ", "pwd", "echo "
        ];
        
        if host_allowed.iter().any(|&prefix| cmd.starts_with(prefix)) {
            return Command::new("sh").arg("-c").arg(command).output();
        }

        // 2. Universal Hardware Sandboxing
        if Self::is_termux() {
            // Termux Node: PRoot Jail
            // Isolates the filesystem root strictly to the current workspace
            Command::new("proot")
                .args([
                    "-r", ".", 
                    "-w", "/", 
                    "-b", "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr:/usr",
                    "-b", "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin:/bin",
                    "/bin/sh", "-c", command
                ])
                .output()
        } else {
            // Crostini Node: Podman Hardened Container
            // Enforces no-network, read-only root, and drops all Linux capabilities
            Command::new("podman")
                .args([
                    "run", "--rm", 
                    "--network=none", 
                    "--read-only",
                    "--security-opt", "no-new-privileges",
                    "--cap-drop=ALL",
                    "-v", ".:/workspace:rw", 
                    "-w", "/workspace", 
                    "alpine:latest", "sh", "-c", command
                ])
                .output()
        }
    }
}

use crate::agent_protocol::AgentAction;
use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use serde_json::Value;

/// Robust extractor that handles most LLM output variations
pub fn extract_actions(response: &str) -> Result<Vec<AgentAction>> {
    let text = response.trim();

    // Strategy 1: Direct parse (clean JSON)
    if let Ok(actions) = serde_json::from_str::<Vec<AgentAction>>(text) {
        if !actions.is_empty() {
            return Ok(actions);
        }
    }

    // Strategy 2: Extract largest JSON array (handles markdown, extra text, thoughts)
    if let Some(array_str) = extract_largest_json_array(text) {
        if let Ok(actions) = serde_json::from_str::<Vec<AgentAction>>(&array_str) {
            if !actions.is_empty() {
                return Ok(actions);
            }
        }
    }

    // Strategy 3: Single object fallback
    if let Ok(obj) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(text) {
        if obj.is_object() {
            if let Ok(action) = serde_json::from_value::<AgentAction>(obj) {
                return Ok(vec![action]);
            }
        }
    }

    // Strategy 4: Aggressive normalization + legacy field support
    let normalized = normalize_action_json(text);
    if let Ok(actions) = serde_json::from_str::<Vec<AgentAction>>(&normalized) {
        if !actions.is_empty() {
            return Ok(actions);
        }
    }

    Err(anyhow!(
        "PARSER_FRACTURE: Could not extract valid actions after multiple strategies.\nPreview: {:.200}",
        text
    ))
}

fn extract_largest_json_array(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let mut best_start = 0;
    let mut best_end = 0;
    let mut max_len = 0;

    let mut i = 0;
    while let Some(start) = text[i..].find('[') {
        let abs_start = i + start;
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut end = None;

        for (j, c) in text[abs_start..].char_indices() {
            match c {
                '[' => depth += 1,
                ']' => {
                    depth -= 1;
                    if depth == 0 {
                        end = Some(abs_start + j + 1);
                        break;
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }

        if let Some(e) = end {
            let len = e - abs_start;
            if len > max_len {
                max_len = len;
                best_start = abs_start;
                best_end = e;
            }
            i = e;
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }

    if max_len > 10 {
        Some(text[best_start..best_end].to_string())
    } else {
        None
    }
}

fn normalize_action_json(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut s = text
        .replace("```json", "")
        .replace("```", "")
        .replace("action:", "\"type\":")
        .replace("\"action\"", "\"type\"")
        .trim()
        .to_string();

    // If it starts with { but is not wrapped in [], make it an array
    if s.starts_with('{') && !s.starts_with('[') {
        s = format!("[{}]", s);
    }
    s
}

use crate::kernel::authority::*;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum CapabilitySet {
    FileSystemRead,
    FileSystemWrite,
    PatchFunction,
    SpawnWorker,
}

pub struct KernelBoundary;

impl KernelBoundary {
    pub fn validate<T>(req: &KernelRequest<T>) -> Result<(), String> {
        if let Some(exp) = req.capability.expires_at {
            if std::time::SystemTime::now() > exp { return Err("CAPABILITY_EXPIRED".into()); }
        }
        if req.identity.actor_id != req.capability.bound_actor {
            return Err("IDENTITY_MISMATCH".into());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub async fn request<T, F, R>(req: KernelRequest<T>, dispatch: F) -> Result<R, String>
    where F: FnOnce(KernelRequest<T>) -> R {
        Self::validate(&req)?;
        println!("[KERNEL_AUDIT] Dispatching trace: {}", req.lineage.trace_id);
        Ok(dispatch(req))
    }
}

use anyhow::Result;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use tokio::fs;
use std::path::Path;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Snapshot {
    pub id: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub hash: String,
    pub directive: String,
    pub timestamp: String,
}

const CATALOG: &str = ".nexus_snapshots.json";

pub async fn list_snapshots() -> Result<Vec<Snapshot>> {
    if !Path::new(CATALOG).exists() {
        return Ok(vec![]);
    }
    let raw = fs::read_to_string(CATALOG).await?;
    let snapshots: Vec<Snapshot> = serde_json::from_str(&raw)?;
    Ok(snapshots)
}

pub async fn take_snapshot(path: &str, directive: &str) -> Result<Snapshot> {
    let content = fs::read(path).await?;
    let hash = fnv_hex(&content);
    let snap_path = format!("{}.{}.snap", path, &hash[..8]);
    fs::write(&snap_path, &content).await?;

    let snap = Snapshot {
        id: uuid_v4(),
        path: path.to_string(),
        hash: hash.clone(),
        directive: directive.to_string(),
        timestamp: epoch_secs().to_string(),
    };

    let mut catalog = list_snapshots().await.unwrap_or_default();
    catalog.push(snap.clone());
    if catalog.len() > 200 { catalog.remove(0); }
    fs::write(CATALOG, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&catalog)?).await?;
    Ok(snap)
}

fn fnv_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut h: u64 = 14695981039346656037;
    for &b in data { h ^= b as u64; h = h.wrapping_mul(1099511628211); }
    format!("{:016x}", h)
}

fn epoch_secs() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_secs()
}

fn uuid_v4() -> String {
    format!("{:x}", std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_nanos())
}

//! Thin async helper so executor.rs can call snapshot logic.
use anyhow::Result;
use tokio::fs;

const CATALOG: &str = ".nexus_snapshots.json";

pub async fn take_snapshot_for_executor(path: &str, directive: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let content = fs::read(path).await.map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Cannot read {}: {}", path, e))?;
    let hash = fnv_hex(&content);
    let snap_path = format!("{}.{}.snap", path, &hash[..8]);
    fs::write(&snap_path, &content).await?;

    let mut catalog: Vec<serde_json::Value> = if std::path::Path::new(CATALOG).exists() {
        let raw = fs::read_to_string(CATALOG).await.unwrap_or_default();
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).unwrap_or_default()
    } else { vec![] };

    catalog.push(serde_json::json!({
        "id": fnv_hex(directive.as_bytes()),
        "path": path,
        "hash": hash.clone(),
        "directive": directive,
        "timestamp": epoch_secs(),
    }));
    if catalog.len() > 200 { catalog = catalog.into_iter().rev().take(200).rev().collect(); }
    fs::write(CATALOG, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&catalog)?).await?;
    Ok(hash)
}

fn fnv_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut h: u64 = 14695981039346656037;
    for &b in data { h ^= b as u64; h = h.wrapping_mul(1099511628211); }
    format!("{:016x}", h)
}

fn epoch_secs() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_secs()
}

use std::collections::HashMap;
use tracing::warn;

pub struct LogicEngine;

impl LogicEngine {
    pub fn linearize_handoff(
        action: &crate::agent_protocol::AgentAction,
        result: crate::agent_protocol::SubagentReturn,
    ) -> String {
        format!(
            "[SYSTEM: DELEGATION REPORT]\nAction: {:?}\nStatus: {}\nOutput: {}\n[DIRECTIVE]: Matriarch, resume execution based on this report.",
            action, result.status, result.output
        )
    }

    pub fn is_action_safe(directive: &str) -> bool {
        let forbidden =
            ["rm -rf /", "mkfs", "shutdown", "chmod 777", "dd if=/dev/zero", "> /dev/sda"];
        let d_lower = directive.to_lowercase();
        !forbidden.iter().any(|&p| d_lower.contains(p))
    }

    pub fn detect_deadlock(observations: &[String]) -> bool {
        if observations.len() < 3 {
            return false;
        }

        let mut read_counts: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();

        for obs in observations {
            if let Some(after) = obs.strip_prefix("[READ_OK] ") {
                let path = after.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
                if !path.is_empty() {
                    *read_counts.entry(path).or_insert(0) += 1;
                }
            }
        }

        for (path, count) in read_counts {
            if count >= 3 {
                let file_progress = observations.iter().any(|obs| {
                    (obs.contains("[WRITE_OK]")
                        || obs.contains("[DIFF_PATCH_OK]")
                        || obs.contains("[PATCH_OK]"))
                        && obs.contains(&path)
                });

                if !file_progress {
                    warn!(
                        "[LOGIC] Localized Deadlock: {} read {} times with zero progress.",
                        path, count
                    );
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }

        let mut last_cmd_sig = String::new();
        let mut cmd_repeat_count = 0;

        for obs in observations {
            if let Some(start) = obs.find("[CMD:") {
                let sig: String = obs[start..]
                    .lines()
                    .filter(|line| !line.contains("Finished") && !line.contains("Blocking waiting"))
                    .collect::<Vec<&str>>()
                    .join("\n");

                if sig == last_cmd_sig && !sig.is_empty() {
                    cmd_repeat_count += 1;
                } else {
                    last_cmd_sig = sig;
                    cmd_repeat_count = 1;
                }
            }
        }

        if cmd_repeat_count >= 2 {
            warn!("[LOGIC] Deadlock: Time-invariant command repetition detected.");
            return true;
        }
        false
    }
}

use tokio::sync::{mpsc, oneshot};
use std::collections::HashMap;

pub enum MemoryCommand {
    Store { key: String, value: Vec<u8> },
    Load { key: String, respond_to: oneshot::Sender<Option<Vec<u8>>> },
}

pub struct MemoryActor {
    rx: mpsc::Receiver<MemoryCommand>,
}

impl MemoryActor {
    pub fn new(rx: mpsc::Receiver<MemoryCommand>) -> Self {
        Self { rx }
    }

    pub async fn run(mut self) {
        let mut db = HashMap::new();
        while let Some(cmd) = self.rx.recv().await {
            match cmd {
                MemoryCommand::Store { key, value } => { db.insert(key, value); }
                MemoryCommand::Load { key, respond_to } => {
                    let _ = respond_to.send(db.get(&key).cloned());
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/**
 * src/metrics.rs — v4.1 Atomic Sovereign
 * Copyright 2026 Donald Ball
 * Lightweight, lock-free, zero-dependency metrics using only std atomics.
 * Fully compatible with Prometheus scraping.
 */
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::LazyLock;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct NexusMetrics {
    pub tasks_total: AtomicU64,
    pub task_failures: AtomicU64,
    pub arbiter_blocks: AtomicU64,
    pub heal_successes: AtomicU64,
    pub heal_failures: AtomicU64,
    pub api_latency_ms_sum: AtomicU64,
    pub api_calls: AtomicU64,
    pub circuit_opens: AtomicU64,
}

impl NexusMetrics {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            tasks_total: AtomicU64::new(0),
            task_failures: AtomicU64::new(0),
            arbiter_blocks: AtomicU64::new(0),
            heal_successes: AtomicU64::new(0),
            heal_failures: AtomicU64::new(0),
            api_latency_ms_sum: AtomicU64::new(0),
            api_calls: AtomicU64::new(0),
            circuit_opens: AtomicU64::new(0),
        }
    }

    /// Increment total tasks processed
    pub fn inc_task(&self) {
        tracing::info!("Task counter incremented");
        self.tasks_total.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Increment task failures
    pub fn inc_failure(&self) {
        self.task_failures.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Increment arbiter blocks (safety interventions)
    pub fn inc_arbiter_block(&self) {
        self.arbiter_blocks.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Increment successful self-healing sutures
    pub fn inc_heal_success(&self) {
        self.heal_successes.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Increment failed self-healing attempts
    pub fn inc_heal_failure(&self) {
        self.heal_failures.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Increment circuit breaker trips
    pub fn inc_circuit_open(&self) {
        self.circuit_opens.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Record API call with latency (used by Orchestrator)
    pub fn record_api_call(&self, latency_ms: u128) {
        self.api_calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.api_latency_ms_sum.fetch_add(latency_ms as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// Compute average latency (integer ms)
    pub fn avg_latency_ms(&self) -> u64 {
        let calls = self.api_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if calls == 0 {
            0
        } else {
            self.api_latency_ms_sum.load(Ordering::Relaxed) / calls
        }
    }
}

pub static METRICS: LazyLock<NexusMetrics> = LazyLock::new(NexusMetrics::new);

/// Returns full Prometheus exposition format text (ready for scraping)

    let m = &*METRICS;

use crate::metrics::METRICS;
use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use futures_util::StreamExt;
use reqwest::Client;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::sync::Mutex;
use tokio::sync::broadcast;

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct ContextPacket {
    pub system_prompt: Option<String>,
    pub model_override: Option<String>,
    pub current_file: String,
    pub current_content: Option<String>,
    pub recent_logs: Vec<String>,
    pub task_complexity: u8,
}

pub struct MicroAgent {
    pub memory: Mutex<VecDeque<Value>>,
    pub tx: broadcast::Sender<String>,
}

impl MicroAgent {
    pub fn init(tx: broadcast::Sender<String>) -> Result<Self> {
        Ok(MicroAgent { memory: Mutex::new(VecDeque::with_capacity(16)), tx })
    }

    pub async fn prepare_and_run(
        &self,
        client: &Client,
        api_key: &str,
        user_text: &str,
        ctx: ContextPacket,
        _resonance: f32,
        model_override: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<(String, u128)> {
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        let model = model_override.or(ctx.model_override.as_deref()).unwrap_or("gemma-4-26b-a4b-it");
        let url = format!("https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse&key={}", model, api_key);

        let combined_text = format!("SYSTEM: {}\nUSER: {}", ctx.system_prompt.unwrap_or_default(), user_text);
        
        let payload = json!({
            "contents": [{ "role": "user", "parts": [{ "text": combined_text }] }],
            "generationConfig": { "temperature": 0.1, "maxOutputTokens": 4096 }
        });

        let response = client.post(&url).json(&payload).send().await.context("API request failed")?;
        let mut full_response = String::new();
        let mut byte_buffer = Vec::new();
        let mut stream = response.bytes_stream();

        while let Some(chunk_result) = stream.next().await {
            if let Ok(chunk) = chunk_result {
                byte_buffer.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
                while let Some(pos) = byte_buffer.iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
                    let line_bytes: Vec<u8> = byte_buffer.drain(..=pos).collect();
                    let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&line_bytes);
                    let clean = line.trim_start_matches("data: ").trim();
                    if clean.is_empty() || clean == "[DONE]" { continue; }

                    if let Ok(val) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(clean) {
                        if let Some(parts) = val.pointer("/candidates/0/content/parts").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {
                            for part in parts {
                                // ⚡ SURGICAL FIX: Forward thoughts to the telemetry stream
                                if part["thought"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false) {
                                    if let Some(token) = part["text"].as_str() {
                                        let _ = self.tx.send(json!({"type": "NEURAL_THOUGHT", "payload": token}).to_string());
                                    }
                                    continue;
                                }
                                
                                if let Some(token) = part["text"].as_str() {
                                    full_response.push_str(token);
                                    let _ = self.tx.send(json!({"type": "NEURAL_STREAM", "payload": token}).to_string());
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        METRICS.record_api_call(start.elapsed().as_millis());
        Ok((full_response, start.elapsed().as_millis()))
    }
}

pub mod task_graph;

use self::task_graph::TaskGraph;
use crate::agent_runtime::engine::{ExecutableAgent, Task, TaskResult};
use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use std::collections::HashMap;

pub struct OrchestratorV2 {
    // ⚡ DYNAMIC DISPATCH: Supports a diverse swarm of agents simultaneously
    agents: HashMap<String, Box<dyn ExecutableAgent>>,
}

impl OrchestratorV2 {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { agents: HashMap::new() }
    }

    pub fn register_agent(&mut self, name: &str, agent: Box<dyn ExecutableAgent>) {
        self.agents.insert(name.to_string(), agent);
    }

    pub async fn execute_graph(&self, graph: TaskGraph) -> Result<Vec<TaskResult>> {
        let order = graph.resolve_execution_order()?;
        let mut results = Vec::new();

        for id in order {
            let node = graph.nodes.get(&id).unwrap();

            let agent = self.agents.get(&node.required_agent).ok_or_else(|| {
                anyhow!("AGENT_MISSING: '{}' not registered in swarm.", node.required_agent)
            })?;

            let task = Task { id: id.clone(), payload: format!("Execute directive for {}", id) };

            let result = agent.execute(task).await?;
            results.push(result);
        }

        Ok(results)
    }
}

impl Default for OrchestratorV2 {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

[FILE: ./crates/runtime_core/src/orchestrator_v2/task_graph.rs]

use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet, VecDeque};

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct TaskNode {
    pub id: String,
    pub deps: Vec<String>,
    pub required_agent: String,
}

pub struct TaskGraph {
    pub nodes: HashMap<String, TaskNode>,
}

impl TaskGraph {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { nodes: HashMap::new() }
    }
    pub fn add_task(&mut self, id: &str, deps: Vec<String>, required_agent: &str) {
        self.nodes.insert(
            id.to_string(),
            TaskNode { id: id.to_string(), deps, required_agent: required_agent.to_string() },
        );
    }

    pub fn resolve_execution_order(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        for node in self.nodes.values() {
            for dep in &node.deps {
                if !self.nodes.contains_key(dep.as_str()) {
                    return Err(anyhow!(
                        "DAG_ERROR: Task '{}' depends on unknown task '{}'.",
                        node.id,
                        dep
                    ));
                }
            }
        }

        let mut in_degree: HashMap<&str, usize> =
            self.nodes.keys().map(|k| (k.as_str(), 0)).collect();
        let mut dependents: HashMap<&str, Vec<&str>> = HashMap::new();

        for node in self.nodes.values() {
            for dep in &node.deps {
                dependents.entry(dep.as_str()).or_default().push(node.id.as_str());
                *in_degree.entry(node.id.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }

        let mut queue: VecDeque<&str> =
            in_degree.iter().filter(|(_, &d)| d == 0).map(|(&id, _)| id).collect();
        let mut order = Vec::with_capacity(self.nodes.len());

        while let Some(id) = queue.pop_front() {
            order.push(id.to_string());
            if let Some(kids) = dependents.get(id) {
                for &child in kids {
                    let deg = in_degree.get_mut(child).unwrap();
                    *deg -= 1;
                    if *deg == 0 {
                        queue.push_back(child);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if order.len() != self.nodes.len() {
            let resolved: HashSet<_> = order.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
            let cycle_nodes: Vec<_> =
                self.nodes.keys().filter(|k| !resolved.contains(k.as_str())).cloned().collect();
            return Err(anyhow!(
                "DAG_DEADLOCK: Circular dependency detected among: {:?}",
                cycle_nodes
            ));
        }
        Ok(order)
    }
}

impl Default for TaskGraph {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

use std::io::{Error, ErrorKind, Result};
use std::process::{Command, Output};

pub struct PodmanShield;
impl PodmanShield {
    pub fn execute(command: &str) -> Result<Output> {
        let cmd = command.to_lowercase();

        // 1. The Ironclad Axiom Block (Never allow self-deletion)
        if cmd.contains("rm -rf src") || cmd.contains("rm -rf .git") || cmd.contains("rm -rf /") {
            return Err(Error::new(ErrorKind::PermissionDenied, "AXIOM_BLOCK: Destructive path."));
        }

        // 2. The Emancipation List (Allow safe host commands)
        let host_allowed = [
            "cargo ", "ls ", "cat ", "curl ", "wget ", "python3 ", "python ", "grep ", "find ",
            "git ", "pwd", "echo ",
        ];

        if host_allowed.iter().any(|&prefix| cmd.starts_with(prefix)) {
            return Command::new("sh").arg("-c").arg(command).output();
        }

        // 3. Fallback Sandbox (Hardened to read-only to safeguard host repository files)
        Command::new("podman")
            .args([
                "run",
                "--rm",
                "-v",
                ".:/workspace:ro", // ⚡ SUTURED: Changed to explicit read-only mode to prevent host code corruption
                "-w",
                "/workspace",
                "alpine:latest",
                "sh",
                "-c",
                command,
            ])
            .output()
    }
}

#![allow(dead_code)] // Will be fully wired in next iterations

use crate::agent_protocol::AgentAction;
use crate::json_parser::extract_actions;
use crate::neural_agent::{ContextPacket, MicroAgent};
use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use serde_json::json;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::broadcast;
use tracing::{info, warn};

const MAX_REACT_STEPS: usize = 12;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum ReActStep {
    Thought(String),
    Action(AgentAction),
    Observation(String),
    FinalAnswer(String),
}

pub struct ReActAgent {
    micro_agent: Arc<MicroAgent>,
    client: reqwest::Client,
    api_key: String,
    tx: broadcast::Sender<String>,
}

impl ReActAgent {
    pub fn new(
        micro_agent: Arc<MicroAgent>,
        client: reqwest::Client,
        api_key: String,
        tx: broadcast::Sender<String>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self { micro_agent, client, api_key, tx }
    }

    pub async fn run(&self, task: &str, ctx: ContextPacket) -> Result<String> {
        let mut history: Vec<ReActStep> = Vec::new();
        let mut step = 0usize;

        let _ = self.tx.send(json!({"type": "REACT_START", "payload": {"task": task}}).to_string());

        while step < MAX_REACT_STEPS {
            step += 1;
            info!("🔄 ReAct Step {}/{}", step, MAX_REACT_STEPS);

            let prompt = self.build_react_prompt(task, &history, &ctx);
            let response = self.call_llm(&prompt, &ctx).await?;

            let thought = self.extract_thought(&response);
            let _ = self.tx.send(json!({"type": "NEURAL_THOUGHT", "payload": thought}).to_string());
            history.push(ReActStep::Thought(thought));

            if let Some(answer) = self.extract_final_answer(&response) {
                let _ = self.tx.send(json!({"type": "REACT_FINAL_ANSWER", "payload": {"answer": answer}}).to_string());
                return Ok(answer);
            }

            match extract_actions(&response) {
                Ok(actions) if !actions.is_empty() => {
                    for action in actions {
                        history.push(ReActStep::Action(action.clone()));
                        let obs = self.execute_action(action, &ctx).await?;
                        history.push(ReActStep::Observation(obs.clone()));
                        let _ = self.tx.send(json!({"type": "REACT_OBSERVATION", "payload": obs}).to_string());
                    }
                }
                _ => warn!("No actions parsed in this ReAct turn"),
            }
        }

        Ok("Task reached maximum ReAct steps.".to_string())
    }

    fn build_react_prompt(&self, task: &str, history: &[ReActStep], _ctx: &ContextPacket) -> String {
        let mut p = format!("You are NEXUS ReAct Agent.\nTask: {}\n\n", task);
        p.push_str("Use Thought → Action → Observation format.\n");
        p.push_str("Available actions: read_file, write_file, vmo_create, diff_patch, etc.\n\n");

        if !history.is_empty() {
            p.push_str("History:\n");
            for step in history.iter().take(10) {
                match step {
                    ReActStep::Thought(t) => p.push_str(&format!("Thought: {}\n", t)),
                    ReActStep::Action(a) => p.push_str(&format!("Action: {:?}\n", a)),
                    ReActStep::Observation(o) => p.push_str(&format!("Observation: {}\n", o)),
                    ReActStep::FinalAnswer(a) => p.push_str(&format!("Final Answer: {}\n", a)),
                }
            }
        }

        p.push_str("\nNext response format:\nThought: ...\nAction: [JSON array of AgentAction] OR Final Answer: ...");
        p
    }

    async fn call_llm(&self, prompt: &str, ctx: &ContextPacket) -> Result<String> {
        let (response, _) = self.micro_agent
            .prepare_and_run(&self.client, &self.api_key, prompt, ctx.clone(), 0.0, None)
            .await
            .context("LLM call failed")?;

        Ok(response)
    }

    async fn execute_action(&self, action: AgentAction, _ctx: &ContextPacket) -> Result<String> {
        let _ = self.tx.send(json!({"type": "ACTION_EXECUTE", "payload": format!("{:?}", action)}).to_string());
        crate::executor::ToolExecutor::execute(&action).await
    }

    fn extract_thought(&self, resp: &str) -> String {
        resp.lines()
            .find(|l| l.trim_start().starts_with("Thought:"))
            .map(|l| l.trim_start_matches("Thought:").trim().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "Thinking step-by-step...".into())
    }

    fn extract_final_answer(&self, resp: &str) -> Option<String> {
        resp.lines()
            .find(|l| l.trim_start().starts_with("Final Answer:"))
            .map(|l| l.trim_start_matches("Final Answer:").trim().to_string())
    }
}

// src/router.rs — Intelligent Agent Router v4.1
// use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum DirectiveClass {
    ShellOp,
    TargetedEdit { file_hint: String },
    RepoDoctor,
    SecurityAudit,
    WasmForge, 
    Inquiry,
    FeatureBuild,
    General,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ContextBudget {
    pub max_file_chars: usize,
    pub max_obs_lines: usize,
    pub max_schema_chars: usize,
    pub max_output_tokens: u32,
}

impl ContextBudget {
    pub fn minimal() -> Self { Self { max_file_chars: 1_500, max_obs_lines: 2, max_schema_chars: 400, max_output_tokens: 1024 } }
    pub fn standard() -> Self { Self { max_file_chars: 8_000, max_obs_lines: 6, max_schema_chars: 1_200, max_output_tokens: 4096 } }
    pub fn doctor() -> Self { Self { max_file_chars: 15_000, max_obs_lines: 10, max_schema_chars: 1_500, max_output_tokens: 8192 } }
    pub fn security() -> Self { Self { max_file_chars: 20_000, max_obs_lines: 10, max_schema_chars: 2_000, max_output_tokens: 8192 } }
}

pub struct AgentProfile {
    pub class: DirectiveClass,
    pub primary_model: &'static str,
    pub max_turns: u8,
    pub budget: ContextBudget,
    pub persona: String,
}

pub struct IntelligentRouter;

impl IntelligentRouter {
    pub fn classify(actual_directive: &str) -> DirectiveClass {
        let d = actual_directive.to_lowercase();
        if ["diagnose", "doctor", "fix repo", "repair workspace", "suture"].iter().any(|k| d.contains(k)) {
            return DirectiveClass::RepoDoctor;
        }
        if ["synthesize", "forge", "wasm cell"].iter().any(|k| d.contains(k)) {
            return DirectiveClass::WasmForge;
        }
        if ["cargo check", "cargo test", "git status", "ls ", "find "].iter().any(|k| d.contains(k)) {
            return DirectiveClass::ShellOp;
        }
        if ["audit ", "vulnerability", "memory safe"].iter().any(|k| d.contains(k)) {
            return DirectiveClass::SecurityAudit;
        }
        if ["fix", "patch", "update", "edit"].iter().any(|k| d.contains(k)) {
            return DirectiveClass::TargetedEdit { file_hint: "target".into() };
        }
        DirectiveClass::General
    }

    pub fn route(directive: &str) -> AgentProfile {
        let start_idx = directive.find("DIRECTIVE: ").map(|i| i + 11).unwrap_or(0);
        let user_cmd = &directive[start_idx..];
        let class = Self::classify(user_cmd);
        match class {
            DirectiveClass::RepoDoctor => AgentProfile {
                class,
                primary_model: "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it",
                max_turns: 8,
                budget: ContextBudget::doctor(),
                persona: "IDENTITY: NEXUS Repo Doctor. Goal: Diagnose and patch compilation errors.".into(),
            },
            _ => AgentProfile {
                class,
                primary_model: "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it",
                max_turns: 8,
                budget: ContextBudget::standard(),
                persona: "IDENTITY: NEXUS Sovereign Agent. Goal: Fulfill the directive.".into(),
            },
        }
    }
}

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

pub struct RuntimeMetrics {
    pub active_tasks: AtomicU64,
    pub crashed_agents: AtomicU64,
    pub emitted_events: AtomicU64,
}

impl RuntimeMetrics {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            active_tasks: AtomicU64::new(0),
            crashed_agents: AtomicU64::new(0),
            emitted_events: AtomicU64::new(0),
        }
    }

    pub fn inc_tasks(&self) {
        self.active_tasks.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

impl Default for RuntimeMetrics {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

use sysinfo::{System, SystemExt, CpuExt};
use std::sync::Mutex;

pub struct SystemMonitor {
    sys: Mutex<System>,
}

impl SystemMonitor {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let mut sys = System::new_all();
        sys.refresh_all();
        Self { sys: Mutex::new(sys) }
    }

    pub fn get_vitals(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
        let mut sys = self.sys.lock().unwrap();
        sys.refresh_cpu();
        sys.refresh_memory();

        let cpu_usage = sys.global_cpu_info().cpu_usage();
        let total_mem = sys.total_memory() / 1048576; // MB
        let used_mem = sys.used_memory() / 1048576;   // MB

        // Attempt to read the ARM64 thermal zone directly
        let temp = std::fs::read_to_string("/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "0".to_string())
            .trim()
            .parse::<f32>()
            .unwrap_or(0.0) / 1000.0;

        serde_json::json!({
            "cpu_usage": cpu_usage,
            "memory_used_mb": used_mem,
            "memory_total_mb": total_mem,
            "temperature_c": temp,
            "timestamp": std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs()
        })
    }
}

[FILE: ./crates/runtime_core/src/task_manager.rs]

use crate::executor::RoboticExecutor;
use nexus_substrate::memory::MemoryPalace;
use crate::{
    agent_protocol::AgentAction, cli_utils, json_parser, logic_engine::LogicEngine,
    metrics::METRICS, orchestrator::Orchestrator, 
    shared_state::VmoState, distributed_scheduler::DistributedScheduler,
    conductor::{Conductor, TurnContext}, router::IntelligentRouter,
};
use reqwest::Client;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::{broadcast, Mutex};
use tracing::{info, error};

// Unified TaskContext for Nexus Singularity v1.9
pub struct TaskContext {
    pub client: Client,
    pub api_key: String,
    pub memory: Arc<Mutex<MemoryPalace>>,
    pub vmo_state: Arc<Mutex<VmoState>>,
    pub tx: broadcast::Sender<String>,
    pub dist: Arc<DistributedScheduler>,
}

pub async fn send_task(
    orchestrator: Arc<Orchestrator>,
    ctx: TaskContext,
    raw_directive: &str,
) -> String {
    METRICS.inc_task();
    let mut session_obs: Vec<String> = vec![];
    let mut history: Vec<(String, String)> = vec![]; 
    let mut turn = 0usize;
    let mut consecutive_fractures = 0usize;

    let _execution_law = cli_utils::get_execution_law_v6().await;
    let mut executor = RoboticExecutor::new(String::new(), ctx.tx.clone());
    let profile = IntelligentRouter::route(raw_directive);

    'mission: while turn < 12 {
        turn += 1;
        info!("=== Turn {} / 12 ===", turn);

        if LogicEngine::detect_deadlock(&session_obs) { break 'mission; }
        if consecutive_fractures >= 3 { break 'mission; }

        let turn_prompt = if turn == 1 { raw_directive.to_string() } 
                          else { format!("The last action resulted in: {}. What is the next logical step?", 
                                         session_obs.last().cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| "SUCCESS".into())) };
        
        let turn_context = TurnContext {
            orch: &orchestrator,
            client: &ctx.client,
            api_key: &ctx.api_key,
            tx: Some(ctx.tx.clone()),
        };

        let response = match Conductor::run_turn(&profile, turn_prompt.clone(), turn, turn_context, consecutive_fractures).await {
            Ok(resp) => resp,
            Err(e) => { error!("Uplink failed: {}", e); break 'mission; }
        };

        match json_parser::extract_actions(&response) {
            Ok(actions) => {
                if actions.is_empty() { break 'mission; }
                history.push((turn_prompt, response.clone()));
                consecutive_fractures = 0;
                match executor.execute_handle(actions.clone(), ctx.memory.clone(), ctx.vmo_state.clone(), ctx.dist.clone()).await {
                    Ok(observations) => { for obs in observations { session_obs.push(obs); } }
                    Err(e) => session_obs.push(format!("EXECUTOR_FAULT: {}", e)),
                }
                if actions.iter().any(|a| matches!(a, AgentAction::Halt { .. })) { break 'mission; }
            }
            Err(_) => {
                consecutive_fractures += 1;
                session_obs.push("[FORMAT_VIOLATION] Output ONLY a raw JSON array.".into());
            }
        }
    }
    "TASK_COMPLETE".to_string()
}

use std::time::Duration;
use tokio::time::sleep;
use tracing::{warn, info};

pub struct ThermalGovernor;

impl ThermalGovernor {
    const CRITICAL_TEMP: f32 = 65.0; // Lenovo Duet throttles heavily at 70C

    pub async fn enforce_cooldown() {
        let temp_str = tokio::fs::read_to_string("/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp").await.unwrap_or_else(|_| "0".to_string());
        let temp_c = temp_str.trim().parse::<f32>().unwrap_or(0.0) / 1000.0;

        if temp_c >= Self::CRITICAL_TEMP {
            warn!("\x1b[31m[THERMAL GOVERNOR] CRITICAL HEAT DETECTED: {:.1}°C. Enforcing 15-second DAG pause.\x1b[0m", temp_c);
            let _ = crate::metrics::METRICS.inc_failure(); // Log a thermal strain as a system fault
            sleep(Duration::from_secs(15)).await;
            info!("\x1b[32m[THERMAL GOVERNOR] Cooldown complete. Resuming operations.\x1b[0m");
        }
    }
}

use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::collections::HashMap;

pub trait Tool: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn description(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value;
    
    /// Executes the tool using the strictly validated JSON payload.
    /// In Phase 2, this will bridge to WASI capabilities.
    fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<String>;
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ToolRegistry {
    tools: HashMap<String, Box<dyn Tool>>,
}

impl ToolRegistry {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            tools: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn register(&mut self, tool: Box<dyn Tool>) {
        self.tools.insert(tool.name().to_string(), tool);
    }

    pub fn get_system_prompt_schema(&self) -> String {
        let mut schemas = Vec::new();
        for tool in self.tools.values() {
            schemas.push(serde_json::json!({
                "name": tool.name(),
                "description": tool.description(),
                "parameters": tool.input_schema()
            }));
        }
        format!("Available Capabilities:\n{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&schemas).unwrap())
    }

    pub fn dispatch(&self, tool_name: &str, input: Value) -> Result<String> {
        if let Some(tool) = self.tools.get(tool_name) {
            // Note: Schema validation logic against `input` will be injected here.
            tool.execute(input)
        } else {
            Err(anyhow!("CAPABILITY_DENIED: Tool '{}' is not registered or agent lacks clearance.", tool_name))
        }
    }
}

use sqlx::{sqlite::SqliteConnectOptions, SqlitePool};
use std::str::FromStr;
use tokio::sync::{mpsc, oneshot};

pub enum MemoryCommand {
    CommitEvent {
        kind: String,
        object_id: String,
        respond_to: oneshot::Sender<bool>,
    },
    CommitArtifact {
        task_id: String,
        artifact_type: String,
        payload: Vec<u8>,
        respond_to: oneshot::Sender<bool>,
    },
}

pub struct MemoryActor {
    rx: mpsc::Receiver<MemoryCommand>,
    pool: SqlitePool,
}

impl MemoryActor {
    pub async fn ignite(db_url: &str) -> Result<mpsc::Sender<MemoryCommand>, sqlx::Error> {
        // Enforce WAL mode for ARM64 IO performance
        let options = SqliteConnectOptions::from_str(db_url)?
            .create_if_missing(true)
            .journal_mode(sqlx::sqlite::SqliteJournalMode::Wal)
            .synchronous(sqlx::sqlite::SqliteSynchronous::Normal);

        let pool = SqlitePool::connect_with(options).await?;

        // MSK Core Schema
        sqlx::query(
            "
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                status TEXT NOT NULL,
                objective TEXT NOT NULL,
                created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
                seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                kind TEXT NOT NULL,
                object_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                ts INTEGER NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS artifacts (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                task_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                artifact_type TEXT NOT NULL,
                payload BLOB NOT NULL
            );
        ",
        )
        .execute(&pool)
        .await?;

        // Bound the queue to 64 to enforce backpressure
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(64);

        let actor = Self { rx, pool };

        tokio::spawn(async move {
            actor.run_loop().await;
        });

        println!(
            "\x1b[32m>> [ACTOR] MSK SQLite WAL Substrate Online. Single-writer active.\x1b[0m"
        );
        Ok(tx)
    }

    async fn run_loop(mut self) {
        while let Some(cmd) = self.rx.recv().await {
            match cmd {
                MemoryCommand::CommitEvent { kind, object_id, respond_to } => {
                    let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
                        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
                        .unwrap()
                        .as_secs() as i64;
                    let res =
                        sqlx::query("INSERT INTO events (kind, object_id, ts) VALUES (?, ?, ?)")
                            .bind(kind)
                            .bind(object_id)
                            .bind(ts)
                            .execute(&self.pool)
                            .await
                            .is_ok();
                    let _ = respond_to.send(res);
                }
                MemoryCommand::CommitArtifact { task_id, artifact_type, payload, respond_to } => {
                    let id = format!("{}_{}", task_id, artifact_type); // Simple compound ID
                    let res = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO artifacts (id, task_id, artifact_type, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)")
                        .bind(id).bind(task_id).bind(artifact_type).bind(payload)
                        .execute(&self.pool).await.is_ok();
                    let _ = respond_to.send(res);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Hash, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Capability {
    ReadFile,
    WriteFile,
    ExecuteProcess,
    NetworkAccess,
    MemoryModify,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct IsolationBoundary {
    pub allowed_capabilities: std::collections::HashSet<Capability>,
    pub run_as_wasm: bool,
}

impl IsolationBoundary {
    pub fn enforce(&self, intent: &Capability) -> Result<(), String> {
        if !self.allowed_capabilities.contains(intent) {
            return Err(format!(
                "SECURITY FAULT: Capability {:?} denied by sandbox isolation.",
                intent
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

[FILE: ./crates/runtime_core/src/v5_engine/graph/mod.rs]
========================================
use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ExecutionNode {
    pub id: String,
    pub deps: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct ExecutionGraph {
    pub nodes: HashMap<String, ExecutionNode>,
}

impl ExecutionGraph {
    pub fn validate_and_sort(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        let mut indegree: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
        let mut sorted = Vec::new();

        // Initialize indegrees
        for (id, node) in &self.nodes {
            indegree.entry(id.clone()).or_insert(0);
            for dep in &node.deps {
                *indegree.entry(dep.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }

        let mut queue = VecDeque::new();
        for (node, degree) in &indegree {
            if *degree == 0 {
                queue.push_back(node.clone());
            }
        }

        let mut visited = 0;
        while let Some(node) = queue.pop_front() {
            visited += 1;
            sorted.push(node.clone());

            if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get(&node) {
                for dep in &n.deps {
                    if let Some(v) = indegree.get_mut(dep) {
                        *v -= 1;
                        if *v == 0 {
                            queue.push_back(dep.clone());
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if visited != self.nodes.len() {
            return Err("FRACTURE: Cyclic dependency detected in DAG. Execution aborted.".into());
        }

        // Reverse to get execution order (dependencies must run first)
        sorted.reverse();
        Ok(sorted)
    }
}

use anyhow::Result;
use wasmtime::*;

pub struct WasmExecutor;

impl WasmExecutor {
    pub fn execute(wasm: &[u8], fn_name: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let mut config = Config::new();
        config.consume_fuel(true);
        let engine = Engine::new(&config)?;
        
        let module = Module::from_binary(&engine, wasm)?;
        let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
        store.set_fuel(50_000)?;

        let instance = Instance::new(&mut store, &module, &[])?;
        let func = instance.get_typed_func::<(), ()>(&mut store, fn_name)?;
        func.call(&mut store, ())?;

        Ok(())
    }
}

// Stubbed for build success - original logic preserved where possible
use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use base64::{engine::general_purpose, Engine as _};
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
use tokio::fs;

pub struct WasmForge;

impl WasmForge {
    pub async fn synthesize_cell(logic_code: &str) -> Result<String> {
        if logic_code.trim().starts_with("const std") || logic_code.contains("export fn") {
            return Self::synthesize_zig(logic_code).await;
        }
        Self::synthesize_rust(logic_code).await
    }

    async fn synthesize_zig(zig_code: &str) -> Result<String> {
        let ts = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)?.as_secs();
        let tmp_path = format!("/tmp/nexus_zig_cell_{}.zig", ts);
        fs::write(&tmp_path, zig_code).await?;

        let output = tokio::process::Command::new("zig")
            .args(["build-exe", &tmp_path, "-target", "wasm32-freestanding", "-O", "ReleaseSmall", "--name", "cell"])
            .current_dir("/tmp")
            .output().await?;

        if !output.status.success() {
            let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp_path).await;
            return Err(anyhow!("Zig compile error"));
        }

        let wasm_bytes = fs::read("/tmp/cell.wasm").await?;
        let b64 = general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&wasm_bytes);
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp_path).await;
        Ok(b64)
    }

    async fn synthesize_rust(_logic_code: &str) -> Result<String> {
        Err(anyhow!("Rust WASM synthesis stubbed for build"))
    }
}

[FILE: ./crates/runtime_core/src/wasm_runtime.rs]

use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use wasmtime::*;

pub struct WasmRuntime;

impl WasmRuntime {
    fn make_engine() -> Result<Engine> {
        let mut config = Config::new();
        config.consume_fuel(true);
        Ok(Engine::new(&config)?)
    }

    pub fn run_bytes(bytes: &[u8], func_name: &str, input: f32) -> Result<f32> {
        let engine = Self::make_engine()?;
        let module = Module::from_binary(&engine, bytes)?;
        let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
        store.set_fuel(50_000_000)?;
        let instance = Instance::new(&mut store, &module, &[])?;
        let func = instance.get_typed_func::<f32, f32>(&mut store, func_name)?;
        Ok(func.call(&mut store, input)?)
    }

    pub fn run_with_buffer(bytes: &[u8], func_name: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Result<f32> {
        let engine = Self::make_engine()?;
        let module = Module::from_binary(&engine, bytes)
            .map_err(|e| anyhow!("WASM_LOAD_FAULT: {}", e))?;
        let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
        store.set_fuel(50_000_000)?;
        let instance = Instance::new(&mut store, &module, &[])
            .map_err(|e| anyhow!("WASM_INST_FAULT: {}", e))?;

        let memory = instance.get_memory(&mut store, "memory")
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("WASM module must export memory"))?;

        let get_ptr = instance.get_typed_func::<(), i32>(&mut store, "get_buffer_ptr")
            .map_err(|e| anyhow!("Missing get_buffer_ptr export: {}", e))?;
        let ptr = get_ptr.call(&mut store, ())? as usize;

        if data.len() > 65_536 {
            return Err(anyhow!("VMO payload exceeds 64KB sandbox."));
        }

        // WASMtime 43+ API: Use .write() directly on the memory slice
        memory.write(&mut store, ptr, data)
            .map_err(|e| anyhow!("WASM_MEMORY_WRITE_FAULT: {}", e))?;

        let func = instance.get_typed_func::<i32, f32>(&mut store, func_name)
            .map_err(|e| anyhow!("WASM_FUNC_MISSING: {}", e))?;

        Ok(func.call(&mut store, data.len() as i32)?)
    }
}

use axum::{
    extract::{Json, State},
    response::IntoResponse,
    routing::post,
    Router,
};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ScrapeRequest {
    url: String,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct ScrapeResponse {
    content: String,
}

async fn scrape(
    // AXUM RULE: State usually comes last or must match the Router's state type exactly
    State(_state): State<()>,
    Json(payload): Json<ScrapeRequest>,
) -> impl IntoResponse {
    // For now, we return a heartbeat to prove the drone is alive
    let response = ScrapeResponse {
        content: format!("Nexus Drone acknowledged URL: {}", payload.url),
    };
    Json(response)
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    // Define the state explicitly as empty tuple ()
    let app = Router::new()
        .route("/scrape", post(scrape))
        .with_state(());

    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:5000").await.unwrap();
    println!("Nexus Scraper Drone ignited on port 5000");
    axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

/// @file
/// @brief Provides `AbslStringify` specializations for types in the LiteRT C
/// API.
///
/// This allows LiteRT C types to be seamlessly used with Abseil's string
/// formatting and logging utilities.
/// @todo Migrate the code in `tools/dump.h` to leverage the Abseil stringify
/// framework.

/// @brief `AbslStringify` specialization for `LiteRtElementType`.
template <class Sink>
void AbslStringify(Sink& sink, const LiteRtElementType& type) {
  std::string dtype_str;
  switch (type) {
    case kLiteRtElementTypeInt32:
      dtype_str = "i32";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeInt64:
      dtype_str = "i64";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeFloat32:
      dtype_str = "f32";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeFloat64:
      dtype_str = "f64";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeInt16:
      dtype_str = "i16";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeInt8:
      dtype_str = "i8";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeUInt8:
      dtype_str = "u8";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeUInt16:
      dtype_str = "u16";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeUInt32:
      dtype_str = "u32";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeUInt64:
      dtype_str = "u64";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeInt4:
      dtype_str = "i4";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeInt2:
      dtype_str = "i2";
      break;
    case kLiteRtElementTypeBool:
      dtype_str = "i1";
      break;
    default:
      dtype_str = ::litert::kNoPrinterTag;
      break;
  }

  absl::Format(&sink, "%s", dtype_str);
}

/// @brief `AbslStringify` specialization for `LiteRtLayout`.
template <class Sink>
void AbslStringify(Sink& sink, const LiteRtLayout& layout) {
  absl::Format(
      &sink, "<%s>",
      absl::StrJoin(absl::MakeConstSpan(layout.dimensions, layout.rank), "x"));
}

/// @brief `AbslStringify` specialization for `LiteRtRankedTensorType`.
template <class Sink>
void AbslStringify(Sink& sink, const LiteRtRankedTensorType& type) {
  const auto& layout = type.layout;
  absl::Format(&sink, "%ud_%v%v", layout.rank, type.element_type, layout);
}

    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflRsqrt:
      op_code_str = "tfl.rsqrt";
      break;

      op_code_str = "tfl.zeros_like";
      break;
    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflResizeNearestNeighbor:
      op_code_str = "tfl.resize_nearest_neighbor";
      break;
    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflLeakyRelu:

    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflCos:
      op_code_str = "tfl.cos";
      break;
    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflElu:
      op_code_str = "tfl.elu";

    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflQuantize:
      op_code_str = "tfl.quantize";

    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflRound:

    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflSelectV2:

      break;
    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflBatchMatmul:
      op_code_str = "tfl.batch_matmul";
      break;
    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflCumsum:
      op_code_str = "tfl.cumsum";

      break;
    case kLiteRtOpCodeTflSign:
      op_code_str = "tfl.sign";
      break;
    default:
      op_code_str = ::litert::kNoPrinterTag;
      break;
  }
  absl::Format(&sink, "%s", op_code_str);
}

#ifndef THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_DETAIL_H_
#define THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_DETAIL_H_

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <functional>
#include <limits>
#include <numeric>
#include <optional>
#include <type_traits>
#include <utility>

/// @file
/// @brief Provides a collection of miscellaneous compile-time and runtime
///        utilities.

namespace litert {

template <typename T>
using RemoveCvRefT = typename std::remove_cv_t<std::remove_reference_t<T>>;

template <typename Cond, typename T, typename... Rest>
struct SelectHelper {
  using type =
      typename std::conditional_t<Cond::value, T,
                                  typename SelectHelper<Rest...>::type>;
};

template <typename Cond, typename T>
struct SelectHelper<Cond, T> {
  using type = typename std::conditional_t<Cond::value, T, std::monostate>;
};

/// @brief A type trait for conditional type selection.
///
/// This works like a sequence of `if-else if-...-else`, where `std::monostate`
/// is the default type if no condition is met.
///
/// Example:
/// @code
///   using TestVal = int;
///   using Test = SelectT<std::is_floating_point<TestVal>, double,
///                       std::is_integral<TestVal>, long,
///                       std::is_class<TestVal>, std::string>;
///   // Test will be `long`.
///   static_assert(std::is_same_v<Test, long>);
/// @endcode
template <typename... Branches>
struct Select {
  using type = typename SelectHelper<Branches...>::type;
};

template <typename... Branches>
using SelectT = typename Select<Branches...>::type;

template <typename... Ts>
struct TypeList {
  static constexpr size_t kSize = sizeof...(Ts);
};

template <template <typename...> typename C, typename... Lists, typename... Ts,
          typename... SoFar, typename Functor>
void ExpandProductHelper(Functor& f, TypeList<Ts...>,
                         TypeList<SoFar...> sofar) {
  ((ExpandProductHelper<C, Lists...>(f, TypeList<SoFar..., Ts>())), ...);
}

template <template <typename...> typename C, typename HeadList,
          typename... Lists, typename... SoFar, typename Functor>
void ExpandProductHelper(Functor& f, TypeList<SoFar...> sofar) {
  ExpandProductHelper<C, Lists...>(f, HeadList(), sofar);
}

template <template <typename...> typename C, typename... SoFar,
          typename Functor>
void ExpandProductHelper(Functor& f, TypeList<SoFar...> sofar) {
  f.template operator()<C<SoFar...>>();
}

/// @brief A utility for specializing a template against the Cartesian product
///        of given type lists.
///
/// The number of lists passed must match the number of template parameters of
/// the template `C`. `C` cannot have non-type template parameters, but this can
/// be achieved using `std::integral_constant`.
///
/// The `Functor` is a callback that is templated on each member of the
/// Cartesian product. It must support a zero-arity `operator()` with a single
/// template parameter.
///
/// Example:
/// @code
/// template <typename LeftType, typename RightType>
/// struct MyStruct {
///   using L = LeftType;
///   using R = RightType;
/// };
///
/// struct MyFunctor {
///   template <typename T>
///   void operator()() {
///     std::cerr << typeid(T::L).name() << ", " << typeid(T::R).name() << "\n";
///   }
/// };
///
/// ExpandProduct<MyStruct, TypeList<double, float>, TypeList<int, char, char>>
///   (MyFunctor());
///
/// // Output:
/// // d, i
/// // d, c
/// // d, c
/// // f, i
/// // f, c
/// // f, c
/// @endcode
template <template <typename...> typename C, typename... Lists,
          typename Functor>
void ExpandProduct(Functor& f) {
  ExpandProductHelper<C, Lists...>(f, TypeList<>());
}

/// @brief In-place initializes an array from a vector.
///
/// This is required if `T` does not have a default constructor.
template <typename T, size_t... Is>
auto VecToArrayHelper(std::vector<T>&& v, std::index_sequence<Is...>)
    -> std::array<T, sizeof...(Is)> {
  if (v.size() < sizeof...(Is)) {
    LITERT_ABORT;
  }
  return std::array<T, sizeof...(Is)>{std::move(v[Is])...};
}

template <size_t N, typename T>
std::array<T, N> VecToArray(std::vector<T>&& v) {
  return VecToArrayHelper(std::move(v), std::make_index_sequence<N>());
}

/// @brief Constructs an object in-place.
/// @see `std::construct_at` from C++20.
template <class T, class... Args>
T* ConstructAt(T* p, Args&&... args) {
  return ::new (static_cast<void*>(p)) T(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
}

/// @brief Checks if a binary predicate holds for all elements of two zipped
///        iterables of the same size.
template <typename LeftVals, typename RightVals = LeftVals>
bool AllZip(const LeftVals& lhs, const RightVals& rhs,
            std::function<bool(const typename LeftVals::value_type&,
                               const typename RightVals::value_type&)>
                bin_pred) {
  if (lhs.size() != rhs.size()) {
    return false;
  }
  for (auto i = 0; i < lhs.size(); ++i) {
    if (!bin_pred(lhs.at(i), rhs.at(i))) {
      return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}

/// @brief Checks if a binary predicate holds for any element of two zipped
///        iterables of the same size.
template <typename LeftVals, typename RightVals = LeftVals>
bool AnyZip(const LeftVals& lhs, const RightVals& rhs,
            std::function<bool(const typename LeftVals::value_type&,
                               const typename RightVals::value_type&)>
                bin_pred) {
  auto neg = [&](const auto& l, const auto& r) { return !bin_pred(l, r); };
  return !(AllZip(lhs, rhs, neg));
}

/// @brief Checks if an element exists in a range.
template <class It, class T>
bool Contains(It begin, It end, const T& val) {
  return std::find(begin, end, val) != end;
}

/// @brief Checks if an element satisfying a predicate exists in a range.
template <class It, class UPred>
bool ContainsIf(It begin, It end, UPred u_pred) {
  return std::find_if(begin, end, u_pred) != end;
}

/// @brief Finds the index of a given element if it is present.
template <class T, class It>
std::optional<size_t> FindInd(It begin, It end, T val) {
  auto it = std::find(begin, end, val);
  return (it == end) ? std::nullopt : std::make_optional(it - begin);
}

/// @brief Computes the average of a container.
template <typename It>
auto Avg(It begin, It end) -> RemoveCvRefT<decltype(*std::declval<It>())> {
  using T = decltype(Avg(begin, end));
  const auto size = std::distance(begin, end);
  if (size == 0) {
    return std::numeric_limits<T>::max();
  }
  return std::accumulate(begin, end, T{}) / static_cast<T>(size);
}

/// @brief Checks if a string starts with a given prefix.
/// @note `std::string::ends_with` is not available until C++20, and
/// `absl::StartsWith` is not portable.
inline bool StartsWith(absl::string_view str, absl::string_view prefix) {
  return str.size() >= prefix.size() &&
         std::equal(prefix.begin(), prefix.end(), str.begin());
}
/// @brief Checks if a string ends with a given suffix.
/// @note `std::string::ends_with` is not available until C++20, and
/// `absl::EndsWith` is not portable.
inline bool EndsWith(absl::string_view str, absl::string_view suffix) {
  return str.size() >= suffix.size() &&
         std::equal(suffix.rbegin(), suffix.rend(), str.rbegin());
}

/// @brief Compile-time strings.
template <size_t Len>
using StrLiteral = const char (&)[Len];

template <size_t Len>
using CtStrData = std::array<char, Len>;

template <size_t Len>
class CtStr {
 public:
  using Data = CtStrData<Len>;

  constexpr CtStr() = default;
  constexpr explicit CtStr(Data&& data) : data_(std::move(data)) {}

  template <size_t N, class I = std::make_index_sequence<N - 1>>
  constexpr explicit CtStr(StrLiteral<N> lit) : CtStr(lit, I{}) {}

  constexpr absl::string_view Str() const {
    return absl::string_view(data_.data(), data_.size());
  }

  //  private:
  template <size_t N, size_t... I>
  constexpr CtStr(StrLiteral<N> lit, std::index_sequence<I...>)
      : data_(Data({lit[I]...})) {}

  Data data_ = {};
};
template <size_t N>
CtStr(CtStrData<N>&&) -> CtStr<N>;
template <size_t N, class I = std::make_index_sequence<N - 1>>
CtStr(StrLiteral<N>) -> CtStr<N - 1>;

/// @brief Concatenates compile-time strings.
template <size_t... Ns>
constexpr auto CtStrConcat(StrLiteral<Ns>... strs) {
  using Out = CtStr<(Ns + ...) - sizeof...(Ns)>;
  typename Out::Data data = {};
  auto cur = data.begin();
  (
      [&]() {
        for (auto i = 0; i < Ns - 1; ++i) {
          *cur++ = strs[i];
        }
      }(),
      ...);
  return CtStr(std::move(data));
}

/// @brief A constexpr-friendly ceiling function.
template <typename T>
constexpr T Ceil(T val, T divisor) {
  return (val + divisor - 1) / divisor;
}

namespace internal {

/// @brief Calls a function `get` and asserts that its return value is equal to
///        the expected value.
template <class F, class Expected, typename... Args>
inline void AssertEq(F get, Expected expected, Args&&... args) {
  auto status = get(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  ABSL_CHECK_EQ(status, expected);
}

/// @brief Calls a function `get` and asserts that it returns `true`.
template <class F, typename... Args>
inline void AssertTrue(F get, Args&&... args) {
  AssertEq(get, true, std::forward<Args>(args)...);
}

/// @brief Calls a function `get` and asserts that it returns an OK
/// `LiteRtStatus`.
template <class F, typename... Args>
inline void AssertOk(F get, Args&&... args) {
  AssertEq(get, kLiteRtStatusOk, std::forward<Args>(args)...);
}

}  // namespace internal
}  // namespace litert

#ifndef ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_LITERT_HANDLE_H_
#define ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_LITERT_HANDLE_H_

#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <type_traits>

/// @file
/// @brief Defines handle classes for managing the lifetime of opaque C API
/// handles.

namespace litert {

enum class OwnHandle { kNo, kYes };

namespace internal {

template <typename H>
inline void DummyDeleter(H) {}

/// @brief A smart pointer-like class for managing the lifetime of opaque
/// handles from the C API.
///
/// This class wraps a `std::unique_ptr` to provide automatic resource
/// management for C-style handles. It supports both owning and non-owning
/// semantics.
/// @tparam H The handle type.
/// TODO(b/477360280): Rename this class to Handle once the migration is done.
template <typename H>
class BaseHandle {
 public:
  using Deleter = std::function<void(H)>;

  BaseHandle() = default;

  /// @brief Creates a new `BaseHandle`.
  /// @param handle The handle to manage.
  /// @param deleter The deleter for the handle.
  /// @param own Whether this object owns the handle.
  BaseHandle(H handle, Deleter deleter, OwnHandle own) noexcept
      : ptr_(handle,
             own == OwnHandle::kYes ? std::move(deleter) : DummyDeleter<H>),
        owns_(own) {}

  /// @brief Returns `true` if the underlying LiteRT handle is valid.
  explicit operator bool() const noexcept { return static_cast<bool>(ptr_); }

  bool operator==(const BaseHandle& other) const noexcept {
    return Get() == other.Get();
  }
  bool operator!=(const BaseHandle& other) const noexcept {
    return Get() != other.Get();
  }

  /// @brief Returns the underlying LiteRT handle.
  H Get() const noexcept { return ptr_.get(); }

  /// @brief Returns the deleter for the handle.
  Deleter GetDeleter() const noexcept { return ptr_.get_deleter(); }

  /// @brief Releases ownership of the handle.
  ///
  /// After this call, `Get()` returns a null handle.
  H Release() noexcept {
    owns_ = OwnHandle::kNo;  // Releasing means we no longer own.
    return ptr_.release();
  }

  /// @brief Returns `true` if the underlying handle is managed by this object.
  bool IsOwned() const noexcept { return owns_ == OwnHandle::kYes; }

 private:
  std::unique_ptr<std::remove_pointer_t<H>, std::function<void(H)>> ptr_ = {
      nullptr, DummyDeleter<H>};
  OwnHandle owns_ = OwnHandle::kNo;
};

/// @brief A specialization of `BaseHandle` for owned handles.
///
/// @tparam H The handle type.
/// @tparam deleter A function pointer to the deleter for the handle.
///
/// @deprecated Use `BaseHandle` instead.
template <typename H, void (*deleter)(H)>
class [[deprecated("Use BaseHandle instead.")]] Handle : public BaseHandle<H> {
 public:
  Handle() = default;

  explicit Handle(H handle, OwnHandle own) noexcept
      : BaseHandle<H>(handle, deleter, own) {}
};

/// @brief A specialization of `Handle` for non-owned handles.
///
/// This class ensures that the managed opaque handle is not destroyed when the
/// `NonOwnedHandle` object goes out of scope.
/// @tparam H The handle type.
template <typename H>
class NonOwnedHandle : public Handle<H, DummyDeleter<H>> {
 public:
  explicit NonOwnedHandle(H handle) noexcept
      : Handle<H, DummyDeleter<H>>(handle, OwnHandle::kNo) {}
};

}  // namespace internal
}  // namespace litert

#endif  // ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_LITERT_HANDLE_H_

#ifndef THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_LOGGING_H_
#define THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_LOGGING_H_

#include <cstddef>
#include <ostream>
#include <string>

#include "litert/c/internal/litert_logging.h"
#include "litert/c/litert_common.h"

/// @file
/// @brief Provides logging utilities for LiteRT, including log interception
/// and formatting.

namespace litert {

/// @brief A tag indicating that a specialization of `absl::Stringify` has not
/// yet been implemented for a type.
static constexpr auto kNoPrinterTag = "!no_printer";

/// @brief Detects whether the current build is a debug build.
inline constexpr bool IsDbg() {
#ifdef NDEBUG
  return false;
#else
  return true;
#endif
}

/// @brief Sets up log interception and reverts it upon destruction.
///
/// This class is useful for capturing logs that are automatically dumped when
/// the C API is called.
///
/// Example:
/// @code
/// Expected<int> DoSomething() {
///   InterceptLogs intercepted_logs;
///   LITERT_RETURN_IF_ERROR(LiteRtCApiFunction()) << intercepted_logs;
///   LITERT_RETURN_IF_ERROR(litert::CppApiFunction()) << intercepted_logs;
///   return 2;
/// }
/// @endcode
class InterceptLogs {
 public:
  InterceptLogs() {
    original_logger_ = LiteRtGetDefaultLogger();
    LiteRtUseSinkLogger();
    ClearLogs();
  }

  ~InterceptLogs() { LiteRtSetDefaultLogger(original_logger_); }

  /// @brief Clears the current default sink logger.
  ///
  /// This is a no-op if the logger is not a sink logger.
  static void ClearLogs() {
    LiteRtLogger logger = LiteRtGetDefaultLogger();
    LiteRtClearSinkLogger(logger);
  }

  /// @brief Streams the intercepted logs to an output stream.
  friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const InterceptLogs&) {
    LiteRtLogger logger = LiteRtGetDefaultLogger();
    size_t sz = 0;
    auto status = LiteRtGetSinkLoggerSize(logger, &sz);
    if (status != kLiteRtStatusOk) {
      return os << "Couldn't get intercepted logs count.";
    }
    const char* sep = "";
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sz; ++i) {
      const char* msg = nullptr;
      status = LiteRtGetSinkLoggerMessage(logger, i, &msg);
      if (status != kLiteRtStatusOk || msg == nullptr) {
        os << sep << "Couldn't get log message number " << i;
      } else {
        os << sep << msg;
      }
      sep = "\n";
    }
    return os;
  }

  LiteRtLogger original_logger_;
};

/// @brief Returns a human-readable string representing the given number of
/// bytes.
inline std::string HumanReadableSize(size_t bytes) {
  static constexpr auto kGb = 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
  static constexpr auto kMb = 1024 * 1024;
  static constexpr auto kKb = 1024;
  if (bytes >= kGb) return std::to_string((float)bytes / kGb) + "GB";
  if (bytes >= kMb) return std::to_string((float)bytes / kMb) + "MB";
  if (bytes >= kKb) return std::to_string((float)bytes / kKb) + "kB";
  return std::to_string(bytes) + "B";
}

}  // namespace litert

#endif  // THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_LOGGING_H_

#ifndef THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_NUMERICS_H_
#define THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_NUMERICS_H_

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <type_traits>

#include "litert/cc/internal/litert_detail.h"

/// @file
/// @brief Provides numeric utilities, including a wrapper for
/// `std::numeric_limits`
///        and helpers for handling exotic data types.

namespace litert {

/// @brief A wrapper for `std::numeric_limits` that can be extended for
///        exotic data types (e.g., quantized types, half-precision floats).
template <typename T>
struct NumericLimits {
 public:
  using DataType = T;

 private:
  using StdLimits = std::numeric_limits<DataType>;

 public:
  /// @brief Returns the smallest positive value.
  static constexpr T Min() { return StdLimits::min(); }
  /// @brief Returns the largest positive value.
  static constexpr T Max() { return StdLimits::max(); }
  /// @brief Returns the largest-magnitude negative value.
  static constexpr T Lowest() { return StdLimits::lowest(); }
};

/// @brief A type trait that provides a wider version of a numeric type
/// (e.g., `i32` -> `i64`, `f32` -> `f64`).
template <typename T>
using WideType =
    SelectT<std::is_floating_point<T>, double, std::is_integral<T>, int64_t>;

/// @brief Widens a given value to its 64-bit equivalent.
template <typename T>
static constexpr WideType<T> Widen(T val) {
  return static_cast<WideType<T>>(val);
}

/// @brief Creates an upper boundary from a value that may exceed the
///        intended data type's limits.
template <typename T>
static constexpr T UpperBoundary(WideType<T> bound) {
  return std::min(bound, Widen(NumericLimits<T>::Max()));
}

/// @brief Creates a lower boundary from a value that may exceed the
///        intended data type's limits.
template <typename T>
static constexpr T LowerBoundary(WideType<T> bound) {
  return std::max(bound, Widen(NumericLimits<T>::Lowest()));
}

/// @brief Flushes denormals or NaN to zero.
template <typename T,
          std::enable_if_t<std::is_floating_point_v<T>, bool> = true>
static constexpr T GetOrFlush(T val) {
  if (std::abs(val) > NumericLimits<T>::Min()) {
    return val;
  }
  return static_cast<T>(0.0f);
}

/// @brief Represents a container element size that supports fractional byte
/// widths.
class ByteWidth {
 public:
  constexpr explicit ByteWidth(size_t numerator, size_t denominator = 1)
      : numerator_(numerator), denominator_(denominator) {}

  /// @brief Returns the number of bytes required for a buffer of a given
  /// number of elements.
  constexpr size_t NumBytes(size_t num_elements = 1) const {
    return Ceil(num_elements * numerator_, denominator_);
  }

  constexpr size_t operator*(size_t num_elements) const {
    return NumBytes(num_elements);
  }

  constexpr operator size_t() const { return NumBytes(); }  // NOLINT

 private:
  size_t numerator_;
  size_t denominator_;
};

/// @brief A trait for number-like types that can be values within a tensor.
template <typename T>
using NumberLike =
    std::bool_constant<std::is_floating_point_v<T> || std::is_integral_v<T>>;

}  // namespace litert

#endif  // THIRD_PARTY_ODML_LITERT_LITERT_CC_INTERNAL_LITERT_NUMERICS_H_
